title: Functions
subtitle: Define, call, local, return vs exit

cards.notes: A black box for a repeating task. Parentheses required after the name.

cards.meaning: Call a function; args become $1 $2 … inside
cards.notes: Same positional rules as a script inside the function body.

cards.meaning: Variable visible only inside the function
cards.notes: Without local, assignments leak into the global shell.

cards.meaning: return N, or the status of the last command
cards.notes: The caller reads $? after the function returns.
Sets the function’s status. Does not kill the whole script.
Unlike return — nothing after this runs in the script.

cards.example: retfunc uses return 1; exitfunc uses exit 1
cards.notes: return → script keeps going. exit → process ends.

cards.meaning: Status is the last command in the function
cards.notes: Caller still sees that status in $?.
